transcript.text: I need to report a significant safety concern from pharmacy. Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. These were near-misses caught during verification, but the pattern suggests the bedside stock in the automated dispensing cabinets is creating confusion between the two concentrations. As a safeguard, pharmacy can remove the bedside stock entirely and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold. This would eliminate the selection risk at the point of care while we work on a longer-term fix.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have an important operational finding from laboratory medicine. Our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this protocol is an aPTT test every six hours. This means nursing and clinical teams need to be aware that aPTT monitoring every six hours — not anti-Xa — will be the lab-supported approach for tonight's shift and through Friday.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From nursing education, I have a critical staffing concern. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Each of these 18 nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they can administer this medication. This is a significant safeguard that needs to be in place before the protocol is used tonight.

decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority electronic medication-record alert at 16:00 today, warning clinicians about concentration selection between 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL and requiring acknowledgment before the order can be released.
